action_summary: Asks the only question the previous round left: with the site GIVEN FOR FREE, can a zero-parameter space over the artifact's own vocabulary and the language's grammar say a real human's replacement, and what does it cost to reach it? Measured on 19 fresh real commits (click, jinja, attrs), mined by a rule and screened before either arm ran, with every commit from the previous 15 excluded by SHA. The census comes first and it is the first result: 10 of 19 are edits of MORE THAN ONE LINE, so half of real fixes are not an expression at all and 'the action' is not atomic. Of the 9 that are single expressions, the base construction (site operands, names in scope crossed with the file's attribute vocabulary, literals, closed under the language's grammar, ordered by ring then size) says the human's expression in 1 of 9, at rank 2887, and the blind search verifies 0 repairs in 32 oracle questions per row over 195 s. Widening the grammar to the four productions the misses actually named (a call, a comprehension, a membership test, a subscript) and admitting the attribute vocabulary of the running interpreter -- dir(str), dir(list), computed in 4 microseconds, stored nowhere -- changes that to 2 of 9 in space with the reachable rank 186,3034, which is the point: closure is what makes the space large. Every one of the nine misses was named, and eight of the nine are closed by three things that are computed rather than stored -- the language's grammar, the interpreter's own vocabulary, and the words the failing test already says -- while the ninth is a renamed attribute that appears nowhere but in the author's head. So the bottleneck is not memory, not addressing, not parameters and not the absence of a model: it is SELECTING ONE EXPRESSION OUT OF THE CLOSURE. One oracle question costs 0.5 s; rank 2887 costs 24 minutes for one line; a value forced into a recorded frame and compared costs 50 microseconds, ten thousand times cheaper and needing no test run. The route this names is the composition of two instruments the tree already owns -- force_the_value_and_see_v1 and expressions_from_a_site_v1 -- with the closure widened by dir() and the ordering replaced by a filter on the demanded value. Nothing here needs a model; parameters_stored is 0 in both arms.

agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: Refused by measurement, in order: the failure text as the index (0 of 15), the flipped firing without a replacement (7 of 7 broke the suite), storing the run (parameters_stored 0 and does not generalise), more vocabulary from the neighbourhood (attributes 115/136 rename-in-place is not a fix), and the statement form (7.5% of edits). What is left is the closure and what selects inside it, which is what this round measures.

obs_solution.efficiency_mechanism: Ordering and exact fit replace breadth: 409 flips decided 15 commits, and no candidate refinement was scored, ranked or thresholded.
obs_solution.generality_mechanism: The rewrite is generic Python AST plus a counter; the oracle is the project's own pytest; the address is a site and a firing, so it carries to any executable artifact.
